questions: Have you noticed any persistent redness or flushing of your face, particularly on the nose and cheeks?
Do you have any sensitivity or burning sensation in your eyes, or any gritty feeling?
Have you noticed any bumps, pimples, or pustules on your face, particularly in the red areas?
Do your symptoms worsen with sun exposure, hot drinks, alcohol, or spicy foods?
Have you ever been told you have rosacea, lupus, or any skin condition before?
Do you have any history of autoimmune disease in your family?
Are you currently taking any medications?
Have you had any recent fever, joint pains, or fatigue?
Do you have difficulty swallowing?
Have you noticed any tightening or thickening of the skin on your fingers, face, or elsewhere?
Do you have heartburn or acid reflux?
Have you been feeling short of breath with normal activities?
Have you noticed any double vision or drooping of your eyelids?
Do you have any hoarseness or changes in your voice?
Have you lost any weight unintentionally?
Do you have any chest pain, particularly with exertion?
Have you had any pain in your jaw when chewing food?
Have you noticed any visual loss or vision loss in one eye that came and went?
Do you have any muscle aches or stiffness in your shoulders or hips?
Have you ever had a heart attack, stroke, or blood clot?
orders: Examine the skin more closely with a Wood's lamp to check for pigmentation changes or telangiectasia not visible in standard light
Perform a slit-lamp examination of the eyes to look for any episcleritis or subtle anterior segment abnormalities
Bilateral hand blood pressure measurement to assess for subclavian steal or vascular asymmetry
Auscultate the carotid arteries for bruits
Examine temporal arteries for tenderness, nodularity, and assess pulsation
Bilateral upper extremity pulse palpation with Allen's test
Full physical examination with focus on the nose - assess structure, palpate nasal bridge, inspect for ulcers or cartilage collapse
Full physical examination - assess for any other skin lesions, lymphadenopathy, or systemic signs
